importantNotes: The book is named for the two censuses (chapters 1 and 26).
Israel's 40 years of wandering resulted from refusing to enter the Promised Land at Kadesh.
The bronze serpent (Num 21) is referenced by Jesus in John 3:14-15.
Balaam's donkey speaks — one of the most unusual events in Scripture.
The Aaronic blessing (Num 6:24-26) is still widely used in churches today.

chapters.1: The first census of Israel's fighting men at Mount Sinai.
chapters.2: Arrangement of the tribal camps around the Tabernacle.
chapters.3: The Levites are set apart for Tabernacle service; census of the Levites.
chapters.4: Duties assigned to the Levitical clans of Kohath, Gershon, and Merari.
chapters.5: Laws about purity in the camp and the test for unfaithfulness.
chapters.6: The Nazirite vow; the Aaronic priestly blessing.
chapters.7: The tribal leaders bring offerings for the dedication of the Tabernacle altar.
chapters.8: Setting up the lampstand; the Levites are purified and dedicated.
chapters.9: The Passover is observed; the cloud guides Israel's movements.
chapters.10: The silver trumpets; Israel departs from Sinai.
chapters.11: The people complain; God sends quail but also a plague; Moses appoints seventy elders.
chapters.12: Miriam and Aaron criticize Moses; Miriam is struck with leprosy.
chapters.13: Twelve spies explore Canaan; ten give a fearful report, only Joshua and Caleb trust God.
chapters.14: Israel rebels and refuses to enter the land; God sentences them to 40 years of wandering.
chapters.15: Additional laws about offerings; a man is put to death for breaking the Sabbath.
chapters.16: Korah's rebellion against Moses and Aaron; the earth swallows the rebels.
chapters.17: Aaron's staff buds and blossoms, confirming his priestly authority.
chapters.18: Duties and provisions for the priests and Levites.
chapters.19: The red heifer ritual for purification from contact with the dead.
chapters.20: Miriam dies; Moses strikes the rock in anger and is forbidden to enter Canaan; Aaron dies.
chapters.21: Victory over the Canaanites; the bronze serpent heals those bitten by snakes.
chapters.22: Balak summons Balaam to curse Israel; Balaam's donkey speaks.
chapters.23: Balaam's first two oracles — he blesses Israel instead of cursing them.
chapters.24: Balaam's third and fourth oracles — prophecy of a star and scepter from Israel.
chapters.25: Israel sins with Moabite women at Baal Peor; Phinehas' zeal stops the plague.
chapters.26: The second census of Israel's new generation.
chapters.27: The daughters of Zelophehad receive inheritance rights; Joshua is appointed as Moses' successor.
chapters.28: Daily offerings and offerings for the Sabbath, new moon, and Passover.
chapters.29: Offerings for the Feast of Trumpets, Day of Atonement, and Feast of Tabernacles.
chapters.30: Laws about vows made by men and women.
chapters.31: Israel's war against Midian; distribution of the plunder.
chapters.32: Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh settle east of the Jordan.
chapters.33: A summary of Israel's journey from Egypt to the plains of Moab.
chapters.34: The boundaries of the Promised Land are defined.
chapters.35: Cities of refuge are established; laws about murder and manslaughter.
chapters.36: Inheritance laws for women who marry within their tribe.
